title: Apply for a security operative licence
summary: Learn about the requirements and process for applying for a Class 1 or Class 2 security operative licence in NSW.
intro:
If you're working in the security industry in NSW, you must hold the appropriate Class 1 or Class 2 security operative licence. You can hold more than one class or subclass on a single licence.

who_can_apply: Be a fit and proper person to hold the class of licence sought.

Have enrolled in, or successfully completed, training with a Security Licensing & Enforcement Directorate (SLED) approved organisation to carry on the security activities for the licence class/es sought.
Be competent to carry on the security activities to which the proposed licence relates.
For further eligibility requirements, refer to Am I eligible for a NSW security licence? – PDF.
what_you_need: A MyServiceNSW Account (you can create one when you start your application).
Two proof of identity documents (one must contain your photograph and may require certification).
Personal details.
Fee payment.

Full Australian birth certificate (not an extract), or Australian citizenship certificate (front and back page), or Australian passport (clearly showing your name, date of birth, photograph, passport number and expiry date), or New Zealand passport (original certified copy clearly showing your name, date of birth, photograph, passport number and expiry date), or an ImmiCard, or a foreign passport (original certified copy only).

A foreign passport clearly showing your name, date of birth, photograph, passport number, expiry date and country of issue and your visa grant notification letter (both must be original certified copies).
A police certificate from each country (other than Australia) you have lived in for 12 months or more over the previous 10 years since turning 16 years of age.
Marriage certificate(s) issued by the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages or, if married elsewhere, the marriage certificate issued by the celebrant or church.
Change of Name certificate issued by the NSW Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages.
Full birth certificate showing your name at birth and your new name (extracts and Commemorative certificates are not acceptable).
Divorce decree.
Deed poll registered with the relevant authority.
Instrument evidencing that the change of name has been registered with NSW Land Registry Services.
Copies of acceptable training documents obtained from a SLED Approved Organisation clearly showing your name, date of issue and the units of competency for Class 1 licences.
A copy of a current First Aid certificate or training qualification with the unit of competency HLTAID011 (Apply First Aid) or HLTAID014 (Provide Advanced First Aid).
If you are an Australian citizen or permanent resident, or a New Zealand citizen, a copy of one of the following documents.
If you hold an eligible visa, you must provide a copy of the required document(s).
If you've changed your name, a copy of one or more of the following.
Evidence of required training units (for certain subclasses).
For Class 1A, 1B, 1C, 1D, 1F licence applicants, provide required training evidence.
For Class 2A, 2D, 2E licence applicants, provide evidence of required training and experience.

how_to_steps.text: Check you meet the eligibility requirements.
Gather the required digital and scanned documentation.Note: You are not able to make any changes online once you've submitted your application.
Log in, or create your MyServiceNSW Account.
Follow the prompts to apply for your security operative licence.

Emails are used to communicate with you throughout the application process. To ensure you do not miss out on important information, you should:
If your application is incomplete, or you fail to provide the required information, your application will be delayed and may be withdrawn.
If your application is withdrawn, you'll receive a refund of fees paid minus the processing fee. After a licence has been issued, there is no provision for a refund of fees.

faqs.q: What licences do I need if I work in the security industry in NSW?
faqs.a: You must hold the appropriate Class 1 or Class 2 security operative licence.

faqs.q: Where can I find out if I am eligible for a NSW security licence?
faqs.a: You can refer to the document titled Am I eligible for a NSW security licence? – PDF.

faqs.q: What is required to apply for a security operative licence?
faqs.a: You must be at least 18 years old, be a fit and proper person, and have completed training with a Security Licensing & Enforcement Directorate (SLED) approved organisation.
